body.p: If a custom framework does not activate in , the problem is usually caused by deployment, framework matching, or framework priority issues. The following checks can help you identify which framework was loaded and why.

section.title: Check the Logs
section.p: Start by checking the server log file at <KIT_DIR>/tomcat/logs/oxygen.log. You can also use the Administration Page to find the log file location and download the log.
At Tomcat startup, confirm that the log contains the line emitted by ro.sync.servlet.StartupServlet:

If your extension is not scanned, it is not deployed where looks for uploaded frameworks. You can also check the Administration Page (in the Frameworks section) to confirm that the uploaded framework is listed there. Also note that frameworks are only scanned at startup, so a full stop and start is required.

section.title: Check Which Framework Was Applied to the Open Document
section.p: To see which framework was applied to the current document, open the user menu and select Report Problem. In the resulting dialog box, check the Document type field. For example:
If the reported document type is not your custom framework, the framework did not match the document. Review the association rules and make sure they identify the intended documents.

section.title: Framework Priority
section.p: In , only one framework applies to an open document. When multiple frameworks match, exactly one framework takes precedence.

The higher precedence is determined by the <priority> setting in the .exf file. The allowed values are Lowest, Low, Normal (default), High, and Highest (the same as in the desktop application). For the general concept and the full value list, see Priority.

Custom frameworks uploaded in user-frameworks that are meant to override a bundled framework (such as DITA or DocBook) should usually set <priority>High</priority> in the .exf file. To avoid ambiguous matches, raise the priority of the intended framework or narrow its <associationRules>.
